messages:
Nora: UX quick sync: opening a thread about the stacktrace overlay. In the current mock, the stack frames are dense and there's no affordance to expand function args. Users want a compact view by default and the ability to expand a single frame. Sketch: https://figma.com/file/redwood/stack-overlay-compact
Samir: Agree. Runtime note: we stream frames with partial symbolication; expanding a frame may require on-demand symbolication which can be slow. Can we show a skeleton loader inline when users expand?
Jules: I suggest a pattern: collapsed frames show function + file:line. On expand, reveal args + source context in a panel to the right (not a modal) so keyboard focus stays within the inspector. Also add a small chevron + visually hidden text `Expand frame` for screen readers.
Anne: For accessibility, ensure expanded panel is reachable by Tab and that focus returns to the frame toggle after closing. Use `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` on the toggle. Sample: "<button aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-controls=\"frame-42-details\">"
Priya: I'll test with VoiceOver to confirm reading order for expanded content. Also recommend avoiding relying solely on color to indicate the active frame; add an outline and text label `Active frame` that is hidden visually but announced by screen readers.
Samir: Dev ETA: skeleton + expand behavior ~2 days. Symbolication API has rate limits so we should debounce expand requests to avoid thundering herd when users navigate frames quickly. I'll add client-side 300ms debounce.
Nora: UX polish: add a `Show source` link that opens source context in a side drawer and a `Copy frame link` small button. Copy should copy `traceid:frame:42` short format. 
deploy-bot: Stacktrace overlay compact mode rolled to staging 2024-06-01T09:30:00Z :rocket:
Jules: Visual note: ensure contrast of code font vs background; use 14px monospace and a 4px left gutter for line numbers. Also add keyboard shortcuts: `E` expand frame, `F` focus frame search. 
Nora: Action items: (1) Samir adds skeleton loader + debounce, (2) Jules updates Figma with expand panel and copy-frame-link affordance, (3) Anne verifies focus management, (4) Priya runs a11y pass on staging. Returning next week with findings.
